newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to retain palm oil export tax - minister.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to retain palm oil export tax - minister.

text.p: Indonesian Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo said on Wednesday the government had no plans to revise the palm oil export tax system.
The palm oil export tax is set by the ministry of finance at the beginning of each month.
"We will retain the present policy and will not change it. This method ensures stable prices," Ariwibowo told reporters.
The government introduced the palm oil export tax in late 1994 to reduce exports and stabilise domestic prices.
A zero export tax in August triggered heavy export commitments due to higher overseas prices. This led to tight domestic supplies and drove local prices up.
The impact led to calls for the government to intervene in the market and to review its tax policy.
Rising exports pushed domestic cooking oil prices to a peak of 1,500 rupiah per kg in late August from 1,310-1,315 rupiah in late July.
A spokesman for the National Logistics Agency (Bulog) said last week it planned to import cooking oil to curb domestic price increases but that the move would only be taken when needed.
It was unclear when imports might start. Ariwibowo confirmed on Wednesday that Bulog might import cooking oil but declined to give other details.
Bulog normally buys CPO, the raw material for cooking oil, rather than finished product as part of its buffer-stock strategy. The CPO is processed by local refiners.

On Monday, the Jakarta Post newspaper said actual CPO production in July and the estimated August figure was 400,000 tonnes and 415,000 tonnes respectively, lower than initial projections of 415,000 tonnes and 455,000 tonnes.
